title: Shayna Gutierrez:
title_short: Shayna Gutierrez · The Youth Is Where It Starts
headline: NIWRC’s newest board member asks the question nobody at the reception had asked yet: who runs the Tribes in 20 or 30 years if nobody invests in the youth now, and what safety needs beyond the Tribe.
story: Shayna Gutierrez is a citizen of the Oglala Lakota Nation from Pine Ridge, South Dakota, and this was her first NIWRC board meeting. Her interview is short (3 minutes) and the strong part is all in the second half: workforce development in Tribal communities is her passion, and her worry is plain: if Tribal leaders do not invest in their youth now, non-Native consultants will be running the Tribes in 20 or 30 years. Her one change for safety is resources that come from beyond the Tribe too, the county and the state.

This is the youth cut of the batch. Her safety definition (“being comfortable in the space that we’re in, not alone”) is good but it is the same lane as Lucy Simpson’s cut, so it stays out. Hopeful, never somber. One voice, hers. The interviewer’s questions are cut out.

Loops: L1 “Who will run the Tribes?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:21 (“invest in their youth now”). L2 “What would she change?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the BUTTON (“the youth for me is where it starts”). Stakes: Tribes run by non-Native consultants who do not carry the culture, the background, the tradition.
